10 Amazing Things Scientists Just Did with CRISPR | List In Post

• 1. Cancer – Modified immune cells taken from the patient's own blood disable a gene that produces a protein that cancer cells normally hijack (October 2016)
  • 2. HIV – Scientists used CRISPR to snip the virus from the cell it was infecting, shutting down the virus's ability to replicate (May 2017)
  • 3. Huntington's disease – Scientists used CRISPR to snip out part of the mutant huntingtin gene that produces the toxic bits (June 2017)
  • 4. Duchenne muscular dystrophy – Used CRISPR-Cpf1, to correct the mutation that causes Duchenne muscular dystrophy (April 2017)
  • 5. Preventing blindness – Editas (a biotech company) is working on a CRISPR-based therapy to reverse the most common cause of childhood blindness. (Paperwork to be filed by end of 2017)
  • 6. Chronic pain – A University of Utah team used CRISPR to prevent cells from producing molecules that lead to the inflammation that causes pain (March 2017)
  • 7. Lyme disease - Kevin Esvelt (Evolutionary biologist at MIT) wants to modify white-footed mice populations to make them immune to the bacteria that causes lyme, thereby preventing transmission to ticks (June 2016)
  • 8. Malaria - Genetically modify male mosquitoes to produce more male offspring, and lower the fertility rate of female mosquitoes (December 2015)
  • 9. Crops - Sainsbury Laboratory (Norwich, England) is looking for ways to remove the genes that make potatoes and wheat vulnerable to disease (No Date Provided)
  • 10. Editing a human embryo - Guangzhou Medical University in China used CRISPR-Cas9 to introduce and then edit out disease-causing mutations from human embryos (March 2017)
